prompt:
A 30-second cinematic episode of an epic space-exploration saga, awe-inspiring and breathtaking, like a nature documentary crossed with a sci-fi epic. This is an ALIEN place — nothing about it should resemble Earth.

The hero: RANGER, the white robot with the rounded helmet and the glowing cyan visor, cyan-lit panels set across chunky white armor, from the first reference image; its fighter-jet form is shown from several angles in the following reference images — note the sharp pointed nose at the front and the engine exhausts at the rear. The golden glyph cube artifact is the last reference image.

LIGHTING RULE: one distant blue-white sun lights everything; consistent light direction and hard shadows in every shot. No moons.

FLIGHT RULE: whenever the jet flies, it always flies NOSE-FIRST — the sharp pointed nose leads in the direction of travel, engines trailing blue fire. It banks and carves like a real aircraft, never drifting sideways or backwards.

THE WORLD — RESPIRA, the breathing planet: the entire crust is one vast living shell and the whole world breathes. Pale ribbed plains of pearl-grey mineral hide swell hundreds of metres upward on the inhale and sink back on the exhale, so its mountains are not rigid rock but flexing plating that rises and falls. Vast slit vents along the ridges open with each breath and blow towering columns of warm white spore-mist into the sky. There is no water and no plant life of any kind — only smooth, taut, faintly patterned living ground stretching from horizon to horizon.

BIOLOGY RULE: the planet breathes on a slow steady cycle, about six seconds in and six seconds out, and EVERYTHING moves with it — the ground lifts, the vents flare open, the mist columns surge, then all of it settles. The rhythm is the same everywhere on the planet at the same moment. Nothing on this world is rigid; every surface flexes under weight.

OPENING (0-3s): deep space. RANGER drifts in orbit above a pale, veined, softly pulsing sphere that visibly expands and contracts like a sleeping animal, mist plumes puffing from ridge vents across the terminator — visibly NOT Earth. A small golden holographic counter floats beside its helmet reading exactly "FRAGMENT 009 / 512". The robot dives.

THE DIVE (3-16s): mid-fall RANGER transforms into its fighter-jet form and drops nose-first. A sweeping continuous flyover: skimming low over rippling pearl plains as a breath-swell rolls under the jet like a mountain being born; banking hard through a canyon of pale ribbed ridges whose walls flex inward and outward around it; punching up through a vent as it exhales, riding the white spore column into the sky; then diving again to reveal the landmark — the GREAT SPIRACLE, a single circular vent kilometres wide, ringed with concentric flexing bands, breathing a slow, kilometres-tall pillar of mist. Fast, fluid, majestic — no slow motion.

THE CHALLENGE (16-23s): RANGER transforms back into the robot and lands on the Spiracle's rim, sprinting down the sloping shaft between the closing bands as the world begins its inhale. The bands squeeze shut in sequence behind it; the floor tilts and rises. A band slams closed early and knocks RANGER off its feet, sliding backward toward the updraft — it fires its grapple into the ribbed wall, hauls itself flat as the mist blasts past overhead, and drops through the last narrowing gap on the exhale.

THE FRAGMENT (23-28s): in the warm hollow at the base of the Spiracle, cradled in a lattice of pale filaments that have grown carefully around it, rests the artifact from the reference image — a single fist-sized golden metallic cube etched with glowing circuit glyphs, rising on a soft column of light. RANGER lifts it. The glyphs flare — and the entire planet takes one enormous breath at once: every plain to the horizon swells, every vent on the world fires a white column skyward together, the whole sphere pulsing gold beneath the tissue.

THE RITUAL CLOSE (28-30s): close-up on RANGER's open palm holding the ONE cube — there is only ever this single cube on screen. Its glyphs pulse and golden holographic text appears in the air beside it reading exactly "FRAGMENT — SECURED" (this exact text, two words only, NO numbers or digits anywhere in it). A calm, epic voice speaks the episode's only words: "Fragment nine... secured." Final frame holds on the robot and the single glowing cube, the pale plain rising and falling slowly behind it.

LYRIC RULE: the singer sings ONLY the four quoted lyric lines below, exactly as written — never any other words. Scene descriptions in this prompt are camera directions, NOT lyrics, and must never be sung or spoken.

Audio: the soundtrack is an original epic MOTIVATIONAL anthem with clear English vocals, composed for this episode — soaring and uplifting, drums breathing in and out with the world through the dive and peaking as the fragment is taken. The voice sings these lyrics across the episode, timed to the action:

"Breathe in, the mountains rise beneath my feet,
breathe out, and every ending is a beat!
This whole world is alive and so am I —
I'll ride the breath of giants to the sky!"

The sung anthem is the only sound until the end, where a calm epic voice speaks the single line "Fragment nine... secured." No other dialogue, no robotic servo sounds. Vertical 9:16 composition, cinematic lighting, photoreal detail on the landscapes, the robot always crisp and readable. Fast-paced, majestic, unforgettable.
